qt: to the Commission Salvatore De Meo (PPE) Subject:

Applying Regulation (EU) 2025/40 on packaging and packaging waste (PPWR) poses significant challenges for the wholesale fruit and vegetable sector. Firstly, businesses that purchase standardised packaging – designed, manufactured and certified by specialist firms – can be classed as ‘manufacturers’ simply by displaying their name or logo on it. This customisation, which is necessary for product identification and traceability, can neither alter the characteristics of the packaging nor justify liability for the compliance thereof. The regulation further fails to specify the frequency of or methodology governing the mandatory compliance tests for maximum levels of PFAS and heavy metals set out in Article 5. Lastly, a draft study ordered by the Commission has proposed that reusable fruit and vegetable crates must be used at least 50 times, with scant regard for hygiene and food-safety requirements. Therefore, in the spirit of the simplification which the Commission is endorsing, can the Commission say: 1.

Whether it intends to clarify that the affixing of a name or trademark does not automatically confer the status of ‘manufacturer’, and what methodology and frequency does it consider appropriate for the checks provided for in Article 5?
What scientific evidence is there to confirm that fruit and vegetable crates that have been reused at least 50 times are hygienic?
Does it intend to establish criteria for their early withdrawal when compliance with hygiene and food-safety standards is no longer guaranteed?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.11.2026) Under the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR)1, if a packaging or packaged product bears a name or trademark, or has a name or trademark affixed to it, the economic operator carrying this name or trademark should generally be considered the ‘manufacturer’. As an exception to this rule, if the economic operator in question is a micro-enterprise, and if the entity supplying the packaging or packaged product is located within the EU, then the supplier of the packaging or packaged product – and not the micro-enterprise – will be considered the ‘manufacturer’ under the PPWR and will need to bear related responsibilities. In relation to Article 5, a stepwise testing approach to enforce the per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) limits is recommended in the PPWR Guidance2. The Commission3 has also developed a common understanding on how the verification of compliance with the PFAS limits should be implemented4 and supports the industry with guidance in the respective part of the Frequently Asked Questions5. The Commission is currently preparing a delegated act to establish a minimum number of rotations for the packaging formats which are most frequently used in re-use6. As the abovementioned Article also specifies, it is obliged to take food hygiene into account when doing so. The Commission will base the draft on the results of the contracted report and will develop it further in close cooperation with the stakeholders thoroughly assessing the available scientific evidence, including in terms of food safety. It is the responsibility of the operator sending a reusable packaging into a new rotation to guarantee its food safety. To this effect the Commission intends to issue guidance for the operators to cope with this requirement.
1 Regulation (EU) 2025/40 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 December 2024 on packaging

and packaging waste, amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Directive (EU) 2019/904, and repealing Directive 94/62/EC, OJ L, 2025/40, 22.1.2025. 2 Commission Notice Guidance document for Regulation (EU) 2025/40 on packaging and packaging waste, C/2026/3702 final. 3 in cooperation with Member States. 4 https://ec.europa.eu/transparency/comitology-register/screen/meetings/CMTD%282026%291190/consult. 5 https://environment.ec.europa.eu/publications/faq-packaging-and-packaging-waste-regulation-ppwr_en. 6 As required under Article 11(2).
